title: Temperature and thermal energy sheet with cooling curve
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Metals and their uses (8G); energy transfers (8K)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 52 (Temperature and thermal energy sheet with cooling curve (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 52: Temperature and thermal energy. To understand the difference between temperature and thermal energy and which way energy flows

questions.q: A cold spoon goes into hot soup. Which way does the energy flow?
questions.a: From the soup to the spoon
questions.model: Energy always flows from hotter to cooler. Soup is hotter, the spoon cooler. So from soup to spoon until they are the same.

questions.q: From the curve, how much did the tea cool in the first 5 minutes?
Why does the tea cool more slowly later?
questions.a: It is closer to room temperature, so energy flows out more slowly

questions.q: Answer the six questions on temperature and thermal energy on the sheet, using the cooling curve.
questions.a: Correct answers (as on the answer sheet)
questions.model: Teacher answers question 1 from the graph: 'after 10 minutes the tea is 49°C'.

questions.q: Explain why your hand feels cold holding an ice cube.
questions.a: Energy flows from your hand to the ice, so your hand loses energy and cools

questions.q: Predict the tea's temperature after 2 hours. Explain.
questions.a: About 20°C: it reaches room temperature (thermal equilibrium)

questions.q: Big question: which melts more ice, tea or a bath?
questions.a: The bath: more mass, so more thermal energy.
